polaris: Can I_phi be pre-registered from input-side spectroscopy, structure, and dephasing variables independently of bulk superconducting output?
framework: Information leakage plus network observability. Treat I_phi as an encoder f_P0(X_pre) with a frozen protocol P0, where X_pre contains only same-sample input-side measurements made before bulk superconducting output Y is inspected.
findings: The predictor/outcome split becomes sharp if I_phi is handled as a zero-leakage code: raw inputs X_pre may enter the encoder, but bulk outputs Y must not enter formula choice, normalization, sample exclusion, threshold choice, or hyperparameter tuning. Under this rule, I_phi is not validated; it is only an auditable pre-registration candidate. The non-circular test is whether an independent auditor can recompute the exact I_phi labels from time-stamped input files while Y remains sealed.

math_object.name: Zero-leakage causal encoder with an input-side observability Gramian
objects: Y = {Tc, zero_resistance, shielding, Meissner_fraction, Jc, bulk_phase_stiffness}
P0 = frozen codebook specifying transforms, frequency windows, normalizations, missing-data rules, and thresholds before Y is opened
Leakage criterion: L_Y_to_P0 = I(Y; P0 | X_pre, calendar_order) must be treated as zero by design, not estimated after the fact

Observability criterion: C_phi is computed from the rank/condition of an input-side transfer matrix mapping interlayer perturbations to optical/spectroscopic/dephasing responses, not from superconducting response
math_object.deeper_structure: This is the noninterference condition from secure computation translated into experimental design: changing sealed output Y while holding X_pre fixed must not change the computed I_phi. The deeper network layer is observability: a phase-bus readiness variable is admissible only if the input probes make the interlayer channel observable before bulk superconducting output is declared.

claim: I_phi can be non-circular only as a frozen input-side encoder; any output-dependent threshold or tuning creates information leakage.

equations.label: F1_candidate_encoder
equations.description: Provisional dimensionless readiness index if Ez2, kBT, hbar*Gphi, and Efloor are all energy scales and Cphi is dimensionless.

variables.Ez2: input-side dz2 interlayer spectral-weight or energy proxy
variables.kBT: thermal energy at the pre-registered measurement temperature

limits.desc: complete dephasing destroys the readiness index

equations.label: F2_blind_leakage_audit
equations.description: Audit residual; pass requires exact equality between frozen labels and labels recomputed from sealed input files before output unblinding.

variables.Ifrozen: I_phi labels deposited before bulk-output unblinding
variables.Irecomputed: labels recomputed by an auditor from X_pre and P0

strangest_prediction.statement: A lower-dz2-weight nickelate sample can outrank a higher-dz2-weight sample if it has a better input-side observability/connectivity factor and a lower independently measured dephasing scale. The ordering is therefore not monotone in dz2 spectral weight alone.
strangest_prediction.specific_system: Same RP nickelate family and same sample batch where multiple films or crystals span apical-O geometry, c-axis optical response, and interlayer dz2 spectral weight without using bulk superconducting labels during index construction.
observables: S_dz2: resonant ARPES or polarization-dependent XAS/RIXS proxy for interlayer dz2 channel weight
W_c: c-axis optical spectral weight integrated over a pre-registered normal-state window
g_struct: apical-O or layer-spacing structural metric from diffraction/STEM refined before output unblinding

Gamma_phi: normal-state dephasing/scattering scale from THz conductivity, pump-probe phase-memory decay, or quantum oscillation/optical linewidth if available, measured above the superconducting-output declaration regime
C_phi: dimensionless observability score from the pre-registered transfer matrix using S_dz2, W_c, g_struct, and Gamma_phi

pass_fail.protocol_pass: Before measuring or opening Tc, shielding, zero resistance, critical current, or bulk phase stiffness, the lab deposits P0, raw X_pre files, missing-data rules, and I_phi labels. A blind auditor recomputes identical I_phi labels from X_pre alone.
pass_fail.protocol_fail: Any coefficient, threshold, sample exclusion, frequency window, or normalization is chosen after seeing Tc, shielding, zero resistance, critical current, or bulk phase stiffness.
pass_fail.physics_pass: Among samples with comparable S_dz2, the sample with lower Gamma_phi and higher C_phi receives higher pre-registered I_phi; if bulk output is later inspected, this ordering is tested as a prediction rather than used to define the index.
pass_fail.physics_fail: I_phi collapses to a monotone relabeling of dz2 weight or c-axis coherence already known in the literature, or only becomes useful after retuning against the superconducting phase boundary.

failed_jumps.jump: Use error-correcting-code distance as I_phi directly
failed_jumps.reason: No clean mapping from physical dephasing in nickelates to a discrete correctable error set without inventing unmeasured syndrome variables.

failed_jumps.jump: Use Granger causality from phase diagrams
failed_jumps.reason: Phase diagrams already contain output chronology and would invite posterior thresholding; it does not enforce same-sample pre-registration.
The experiment observes an existing material rather than actuating all hidden interlayer states; observability is the sharper requirement for an input-side index.

claims.statement: The decisive S1 criterion is noninterference: holding X_pre fixed, changing sealed bulk output Y must not change I_phi, thresholds, or inclusion rules.

equations.label: F1_candidate_encoder
equations.description: Frozen input-side encoder candidate; not validated as a predictor.

assumptions: X_pre files are time-stamped and sealed before bulk superconducting output is opened.
P0 fixes all transforms, windows, weights, thresholds, and missing-data rules before output inspection.
Gamma_phi is measured from normal-state or otherwise input-side dephasing data, not inferred from superconducting stiffness or transition width.

claims.statement: C_phi should be treated as an input-side network observability score, not as observed bulk phase coherence.

equations.label: F3_observability_score
equations.description: Dimensionless stability score from the smallest singular value of the pre-registered input-side transfer matrix.

variables.sigma_min: smallest singular value of the input-side transfer matrix after fixed normalization
variables.sigma_ref: pre-registered reference scale preventing singular blow-up

assumptions: The transfer matrix uses only pre-output observables such as S_dz2, W_c, structure, and Gamma_phi.
Normalization of rows and singular values is frozen before output unblinding.
C_phi is not allowed to include Josephson-like bulk phase stiffness.
Same-sample input measurements are feasible before bulk superconducting output declaration.
Normal-state or input-side dephasing measurements can be separated operationally from bulk superconducting output variables.
The experiment can maintain a blind data workflow with sealed output labels.
The goal is a non-circular protocol, not validation of I_phi.
weakest_point: Gamma_phi is the most fragile variable: many experimentally accessible linewidths mix ordinary scattering, disorder, and incipient superconducting fluctuations. If Gamma_phi cannot be measured without borrowing bulk phase-stiffness or transition information, the candidate I_phi fails the S1 split.
next_plan: Round 2 should stress-test the observability construction: define the exact transfer-matrix rows, units, normalization, and missing-data rules, then ask whether any row secretly encodes superconducting output. A second route should test whether a minimal preregistration packet can be specified for three blind samples before unblinding Y.

inspector_check.formula: I_phi = Ez2*Cphi/(kBT + hbar*Gphi + Efloor); all denominator terms must be energies and Cphi dimensionless.
inspector_check.direction: Increasing Ez2 or Cphi raises I_phi; increasing Gphi, temperature energy, or Efloor lowers I_phi.
inspector_check.data: No bulk superconducting output data used in this B Round 1 construction.
inspector_check.assumptions: P0 and X_pre are sealed before output unblinding; Cphi is an input-side observability score.
